root_cause.text: The endianness conversion logic in scarlett2_usb_get_config() checks the total buffer size (`size`) instead of the individual element size (`config_item->size`), causing incorrect loop bounds when converting multi-element arrays and leading to buffer overflow.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `if (size == 2)` to `if (config_item->size == 16)` and from `else if (size == 4)` to `else if (config_item->size == 32)`. The CVE description explicitly states: "The code checks `if (size == 2)` where `size` is the total buffer size in bytes, then loops `count` times treating each element as u16 (2 bytes). This causes the loop to access `count * 2` bytes when the buffer only has `size` bytes allocated." By checking `config_item->size` (the element size in bits) instead of `size` (total buffer size in bytes), the conversion correctly applies to each element regardless of the count value.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present at line 1189. The code checks `if (size == 2)` where `size` is the total buffer size in bytes (calculated as `config_item->size / 8 * count` at line 1185). However, the endianness conversion loop at lines 1192-1193 iterates `count` times, which is the number of elements. The bug occurs because the condition should check `config_item->size == 2` (the individual element size in bits) instead of `size == 2` (the total buffer size). When `count > 1` and `size == 2`, the loop will iterate multiple times but only 2 bytes total are available, causing a buffer overflow. The fix would require checking the individual element size (`config_item->size`) rather than the total size (`size`), which is not present in this code.
